Though the injury has been opined to be grievous, there is nothing on record to show that the injury was grievous in nature as the doctor has not even prescribed admission or necessity to admit the patient.
In these circumstances, the injuries sustained by the victim are considered to be simple in nature.
Considering the nature of injury, it is assumed that the petitioner may have remained bedridden for not more than 15 days.
20. Petitioner Mohd. Amir has claimed to be working as a reporter with Bihari Khabar News Agency at a salary of Rs.18,000/- per month.
In order to prove the same he has relied upon his ID Card issued by his employer as Ex.PW1/D and a certificate as Ex.PW1/E.

It is pertinent to note that as per Ex.PW1/E, the alleged employer has certified that the victim had worked in his office from 01.12.2018 till 31.12.2019 and had left the office w.e.f 01.01.2021 i.e. 9 days before the date of accident CHARU
by CHARU GUPTA GUPTA
It is also noticed that the ID card Ex.PW1/D has bee issued on 01.01.2021 i.e. the date when the victim had allegedly left the office.
In these circumstances, neither PW1/D nor PW1/E can be relied upon as a true proof of employment or income.
Victim has not filed any other proof of employment, salary or educational qualification.
As such, his notional income has to be assessed on the basis of minimum wages of an unskilled labour applicable in Delhi i.e. Rs.15310/- per month which is Rs.510/- per day.
Accordingly, petitioner is entitled to compensation towards loss of income equivalent to Rs.510X15= Rs.7650/-.
21. Claimant not filed any original documents.
Hence, considering the injuries of the injured petitioner is granted Rs.10,000/- for his medical treatment.
No compensation towards future loss of income can be granted in cases where petitioner has not proved to have sustained any permanent disability.
